children: Mothercare shares plummeted as it warned its future was highly uncertain, after a Middle East franchise partner said it expects to close most of its stores in the region due to the Iran war.
Shares were down 68% at 25 pence in morning London trade. Over the year to date, they are down 90%.
The U.K. baby-products retailer said Friday that it expects a material fall in orders in the year through March 2028, which will result in a similar hit to revenues, profits and cash flows.

The retailer said it has enough resources to trade for a number of months, but warned its longer-term solvency remains highly uncertain. It has initiated a strategic review of its business model and costs.

The warning comes after one of its main partners in the Middle East said it has launched a review of its Mothercare franchise stores. While the review is yet to conclude, the partner has indicated it expects to close the majority of its stores in 2027.
The Middle East conflict, which has dented consumer sentiment in the region, shows no sign of ending soon.
